title: Thorn and Veil
premise: Yara Dunmore, a cartographer who has spent his life mapping the unmapped valley where magic cannot follow, is pulled into the wider world when a mute child arrives at his door speaking a language older than any kingdom. The child's soul has been sold to the court beneath the mountain, and the debt comes due when the moon completes its thirteenth turn. To save him, Yara must cross realms he has only ever drawn from rumor, ally with outlaws and exiles who keep justice outside the law, and confront the truth that he himself was born of magic — the reason the valley cannot hold it. In the end, Yara trades his own claim to belonging for the child's freedom, rewriting the map so that no court, above or below, can ever buy a soul again.
about_author: August Halloran is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent a decade drawing boundaries for land he never owned. Thorn and Veil is his second novel, written in the margins of old maps he refuses to sell.

chapters.title: The Valley That Refuses
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He surveys the valley's edge where his instruments fail and ink runs pale, establishing his obsession with maps and his fear of leaving. Emotional beat: restless contentment about to crack.

chapters.title: A Knock at Dusk
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A mud-caked boy appears at his door, mute except for words in an impossible language. When Yara touches him, the compass needle spins wild. Beat: wonder laced with dread.

chapters.title: Words Older Than Stone
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. An elderly herbwoman, Maren, recognizes fragments of the tongue as pre-kingdom speech and warns that its speakers are 'owned.' Beat: first hint of the debt.

chapters.title: The Mark Beneath the Skin
chapters.summary: Child's POV (rendered through Yara's observation). Yara finds a sigil branded under the boy's collarbone — a contract mark. Beat: protective fury ignites.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She deciphers the sigil: the boy's soul was sold to the Court Beneath the Mountain; the debt matures on the thirteenth turning of the moon. Beat: cold clarity — twelve turns remain.

chapters.title: Leaving the Map
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He crosses the valley's boundary for the first time; magic floods back into the world like color after blindness, and it terrifies him. Beat: vertigo and exhilaration.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Yara and the boy travel toward the mountain, bartering map-drawing skills for passage. Beat: tentative trust forming between them.

chapters.title: Thieves Who Keep the Peace
chapters.summary: Outlaw captain Sef's POV. Her band ambushes them but spares the pair upon seeing the contract mark — they hunt soul-brokers too. Beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Around the fire she explains how courts sold justice centuries ago; her band enforces their own. Yara bristles at lawlessness yet sees its fairness. Beat: ideology challenged.

chapters.title: First Turning
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. One moon gone. The boy speaks his first common word: 'home.' Beat: tenderness sharpening stakes.

chapters.title: The Broker's Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. They raid a tollhouse where souls are weighed and find records naming the boy's seller — someone from Yara's own valley. Beat: betrayal foreshadowed.

chapters.title: Ink and Iron
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. His cartography proves magical here: maps he draws become briefly true terrain. The outlaws realize his worth. Beat: identity as power discovered.

chapters.title: The Veiled Market
chapters.summary: Child's POV, dreamlike. The boy leads them to a hidden market of veiled traders who deal in names and memories. Beat: uncanny wonder.

chapters.title: Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. To learn the mountain's gates, Yara must trade a memory — he gives up his mother's face. Beat: grief as currency.

chapters.title: Second Turning
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Two moons gone; the band fractures over whether the mission is suicide. Beat: loyalty tested.

chapters.title: The River That Remembers
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Crossing a river that replays the past, Yara glimpses his own infancy outside the valley — held by hands that glowed. Beat: origin mystery deepens.

chapters.title: Hollow Men of the Pass
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Soul-broker enforcers attack; the band loses a member, Bram. Beat: cost made flesh, resolve hardened.

chapters.title: What Bram Carried
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Sorting Bram's effects, Yara finds a map fragment in his own childhood handwriting — one he never drew. Beat: dread and compulsion.

chapters.title: Third Turning
chapters.summary: Child's POV. The boy begins remembering his stolen life in dreams, weeping without sound. Beat: innocence bearing adult grief.

chapters.title: The City of Permitted Streets
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They pass through a lawful city where everything is licensed, surveilled, taxed — a mirror of the court they fight. Beat: theme crystallized.

chapters.title: A Favor Owed by the Queen's Exile
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. They seek a disgraced court mage, Ilvane, exiled for refusing to weigh souls. She agrees to help — for a future favor unnamed. Beat: uneasy bargain.

chapters.title: Ilvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Ilvane's POV. She reveals the valley exists because someone walled magic out — and that wall has a maker. Beat: revelation aimed at Yara.

chapters.title: Fourth Turning
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Halfway. His traded memory returns in fragments: his mother's voice saying 'the veil was for you.' Beat: suspicion turned inward.

chapters.title: The Wall's Architect
chapters.summary: Ilvane's POV. She confirms Yara's parents built the valley's veil to hide him from the court — he is a soul the brokers never stopped hunting. Beat: identity upended.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Ashwood
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Hunted now in earnest, the company flees through a burned forest where broker hounds track souls. Beat: relentless pursuit.

chapters.title: The Boy Chooses
chapters.summary: Child's POV. Offered escape by the hounds' master if he abandons Yara, the boy refuses — his first full sentence in years. Beat: agency reclaimed.

chapters.title: Fifth Turning
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Grief and gratitude braided; he begins drafting a new kind of map — one that could unmake contracts. Beat: purpose forged.

chapters.title: The Gate of Teeth
chapters.summary: Ilvane's POV. They reach the mountain's gate, which admits only those who name their true desire. Each answer costs honesty. Beat: naked truths exchanged.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Descent into the court: a cathedral of ledgers where souls hang like lanterns. Beat: awe curdled into horror.

chapters.title: Audience with the Under-Crown
chapters.summary: Under-Crown's POV. The court's ruler offers Yara his parents' fate and his own belonging in exchange for the boy. Beat: temptation precisely tailored.

chapters.title: Sixth Turning
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Above ground, the outlaws prepare a diversion as the moon nears completion; Sef chooses to stay despite orders to flee. Beat: chosen family affirmed.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Debt
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The contract is read aloud; Yara discovers a clause — a soul may be redeemed by an equal claim. He has none. Beat: despair at the letter of the law.

chapters.title: Cartography as Rebellion
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Working through the night, Yara draws a map of the court itself — and because his maps become true, the walls begin to shift. Beat: ingenuity as climax approach.

chapters.title: Seventh Turning: Eclipse
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The thirteenth moon rises eclipsed; the diversion erupts; Ilvane pays her unnamed favor by holding the gate. Beat: all threads taut.

chapters.title: The Claim of the Unmapped
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Before the Under-Crown, Yara claims the boy not by law but by map: territory drawn and named belongs to its mapper. He names the boy's soul his own country. Beat: defiant triumph.

chapters.title: What the Court Cannot Buy
chapters.summary: Under-Crown's POV. Enraged, the court tries to seize Yara's soul as payment — but a soul that has renounced belonging cannot be collateral. The contract unravels. Beat: thematic resolution through sacrifice.

chapters.title: Lanterns Going Home
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The hanging souls are freed; the boy's returns to him and he speaks his true name aloud. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: The Redrawn Valley
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Yara redraws the valley's boundary — open now, warded against brokers rather than magic. The outlaws ride with them home. Beat: belonging redefined, not abandoned.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn, Complete
chapters.summary: Child's POV. On the night the debt would have come due, the boy sleeps soundly in Yara's house while the moon passes whole overhead. Beat: peace earned.

chapters.title: Margins and Blank Spaces
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Epilogue: Yara publishes a new atlas with deliberate blank spaces, writing that some places belong to those who live there, not those who draw them. Beat: quiet, hopeful close.
